A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same speech-summarization survey. Their main text, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: v2 reports original descriptive analyses of publication trends, evaluation-metric usage, and publication venues in Figures 1, B1, and D1. These qualify as data-analysis results.

after.justification: v3 retains those original bibliometric analyses. Its new Table 3 separately compiles performance results attributed to prior studies.

M1.justification: Neither version proposes a new summarization algorithm. The change from no projector to a trainable linear projector for Chu et al. (2024) revises the description of an existing surveyed model; it does not establish an actual method modification.

E1.justification: FLORAS 50 and MCIF enter Table 1, and MACSum enters Table A3 as catalogued resources. These additions do not constitute datasets newly used for training or evaluation by this work. Table 3 synthesizes previously published How2 experiments.

E2.justification: Table 3 newly lists cascaded baselines alongside end-to-end models from cited studies. Neither version evaluates a proposed method against baselines, and no comparator membership changes are established for the work's own analyses.

E3.justification: Table 3 newly documents input limits, parameter counts, augmentation, and metrics for existing published experiments. It does not revise their protocols or report new experimental execution. The survey's bibliometric normalization and evaluation-method descriptions remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 3 adds limited sensitivity and ablation evidence from prior studies: Miyazaki et al.'s 96M Mamba-Transformer with 100 versus 600 seconds of input, and Matsuura et al.'s 203M Conformer-Transformer with versus without TTS augmentation. These comparisons were absent from v2; no new robustness experiments are reported.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance testing for its analyses. Table 3 adds point scores without introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Section 6.3 and Table 3 introduce the survey's first systematic model-performance synthesis, reporting ROUGE-L and BERTScore for five cascaded and fifteen end-to-end configurations. For example, Chen et al.'s full-input Conformer-Transformer (Flash) is listed at 65.5 and 93.9. These are newly included published results, not version-to-version performance gains. Existing bibliometric results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The conceptual problem formulation is retained. Neither version introduces mathematical definitions, theorems, proofs, or formal derivations that change between versions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, survey scope, and conclusion retain the same central contribution: synthesizing speech-summarization resources, evaluation, and modeling approaches while identifying multilingual, benchmark, and long-context challenges.

C2.justification: Section 6.3 adds interpretations linking performance to context length, parameter count, and synthetic speech. Section 7 expands multilingual and cross-lingual applicability constraints. Ethical Considerations adds specific mechanisms connecting demographic ASR disparities and disfluencies to downstream summary bias. Existing limitations are retained.

D1.justification: Table 2 and Section 6.2.2 revise Qwen2-Audio's projector and trainability documentation. Table 3 supplies input-duration, parameter-count, TTS-augmentation, and zero-shot details for cited experiments. New resource entries include access links and licensing information, and Section 4 adds an interactive dataset-catalogue link.

R1.justification: v3 expands cited literature on multilingual resources, cross-lingual summarization, controllable summaries, podcast previews, and disfluency/fairness, including FLORAS 50, MCIF, MACSum, and Teleki et al. (2024). These are focused extensions within the retained research positioning. Publication-metadata updates and removal of the duplicate MoverScore reference do not represent new works.

P1.justification: v3 adds Section 6.3, expands selected discussion paragraphs, and separates multilingual/cross-lingual discussion within Section 7. It also corrects wording and headings such as 'Synthetic Data' and 'Dataset Derivatives and Augmentations.' The overall section sequence and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds the visually grouped performance Table 3 and expands Tables 1 and A3 with new resource rows. Table widths, footnotes, and surrounding text reflow locally. Figures 1, 2, B1, and D1 retain their displays, and the appendix evaluation tables retain their organization.

improvement.justification: v3 resolves the internally inconsistent Qwen2-Audio projector description and improves the survey's usefulness through explicit performance/settings comparisons and additional multilingual resource documentation. The fairness discussion also provides more concrete mechanisms of bias propagation. The gains remain limited because Table 3 combines heterogeneous published settings on How2, restricting the strength of its broader performance interpretations.
